Project Python Foundations: FoodHub Data Analysis¶

Marks: 60

Context¶

The number of restaurants in New York is increasing day by day. Lots of students and busy professionals rely on those restaurants due to their hectic lifestyles. Online food delivery service is a great option for them. It provides them with good food from their favorite restaurants. A food aggregator company FoodHub offers access to multiple restaurants through a single smartphone app.

The app allows the restaurants to receive a direct online order from a customer. The app assigns a delivery person from the company to pick up the order after it is confirmed by the restaurant. The delivery person then uses the map to reach the restaurant and waits for the food package. Once the food package is handed over to the delivery person, he/she confirms the pick-up in the app and travels to the customer's location to deliver the food. The delivery person confirms the drop-off in the app after delivering the food package to the customer. The customer can rate the order in the app. The food aggregator earns money by collecting a fixed margin of the delivery order from the restaurants.

Objective¶

The food aggregator company has stored the data of the different orders made by the registered customers in their online portal. They want to analyze the data to get a fair idea about the demand of different restaurants which will help them in enhancing their customer experience. Suppose you are hired as a Data Scientist in this company and the Data Science team has shared some of the key questions that need to be answered. Perform the data analysis to find answers to these questions that will help the company to improve the business.

Data Description¶

The data contains the different data related to a food order. The detailed data dictionary is given below.

Data Dictionary¶

  • order_id: Unique ID of the order
  • customer_id: ID of the customer who ordered the food
  • restaurant_name: Name of the restaurant
  • cuisine_type: Cuisine ordered by the customer
  • cost: Cost of the order
  • day_of_the_week: Indicates whether the order is placed on a weekday or weekend (The weekday is from Monday to Friday and the weekend is Saturday and Sunday)
  • rating: Rating given by the customer out of 5
  • food_preparation_time: Time (in minutes) taken by the restaurant to prepare the food. This is calculated by taking the difference between the timestamps of the restaurant's order confirmation and the delivery person's pick-up confirmation.
  • delivery_time: Time (in minutes) taken by the delivery person to deliver the food package. This is calculated by taking the difference between the timestamps of the delivery person's pick-up confirmation and drop-off information

Overall Observations for Question 6:¶

  • The order ID's are evenly distributed with no outliers.
  • The average cost of order is $16.50.
  • The variables show that some categories are considerably more common than others, indicating that customer orders are not evenly distributed across all categories.
  • The order cost and delivery time distributions show noticeable variation, meaning customers experience different order prices and delivery durations.
  • This data provides critical overview and information of customer ordering patterns and FoodHub's operational characteristics, particularly in terms of cuisine preferences, spending, preparation time, and delivery time.

labels = ['Orders > $20', 'Orders <= $20']

Question 14: The company charges the restaurant 25% on the orders having cost greater than 20 dollars and 15% on the orders having cost greater than 5 dollars. Find the net revenue generated by the company across all orders. [3 marks]¶

def calculate_revenue(cost):
    if cost > 20:
        return cost * 0.25
    elif cost > 5:
        return cost * 0.15
    else:
        return 0

df['revenue'] = df['cost_of_the_order'].apply(calculate_revenue)

net_revenue = df['revenue'].sum()

from scipy.stats import ttest_ind

weekday = df[df['day_of_the_week'] == 'Weekday']['delivery_time']
weekend = df[df['day_of_the_week'] == 'Weekend']['delivery_time']

t_stat, p_value = ttest_ind(weekday, weekend, equal_var=False)

print("T-statistic:", t_stat)
print("P-value:", p_value)

T-statistic: 33.262190207973624
P-value: 2.5737146093950945e-184

Observations:¶

  • During the weekday, it typically takes longer for delivery.
  • There is a bigger difference between the wait times for delivery on the weekends.
  • Orders take almost 6 minutes longer to deliver on weekdays than on weekends.
  • Overall, delivery times are faster on weekends than on weekdays.
  • Mean delivery time on weekdays is 28 minutes and on weekends it is 22 minutes.
  • The minimum and maximum time for delivery is more consistent than the minimum and maximum time for delivery on the weekends.
  • The fastest delivery occurs on weekends (15 minutes), which is 9 minutes faster than the fastest weekday delivery.

Conclusion and Recommendations for question 16¶

  • Investigate why weekday deliveries take longer than weekend deliveries.
  • FoodHub might want to increase the number of delivery drivers on weekdays.
  • FoodHub could focus on improving restaurant preparation and delivery coordination during weekdays.
  • FoodHub should monitor weekday and weekend delivery times to determine whether operational changes that are made are improving performance.

Question 17: What are your conclusions from the analysis? What recommendations would you like to share to help improve the business? (You can use cuisine type and feedback ratings to drive your business recommendations.) [6 marks]¶

Conclusions:¶

  • A lot of customers do not provide ratings.
  • Delivery times varied greatly on the weekends.
  • The cuisine types that are most popular are American, Japanese, and Italian.
  • There is a large cost difference between cuisines.
  • Food delivery and preparation times do not impact customer rating much.
  • There is a statistically significant difference in delivery times between weekdays and weekends. The t-test produced a t-statistic of 33.262190207973624 and a p-value of 2.5737146093950945e-184. This is way below the 5% significance level.
  • Most of the orders are reasonably priced.
  • FoodHub has a large customer base, with 1,898 orders from 1,200 unique customers and 178 restaurants across 14 different cuisine types.
  • Customers have a wide variety of cuisine types to choose from.
  • Delivery time is the area that FoodHub should work the hardest to improve.

Recommendations:¶

  • FoodHub could offer customers loyalty points or a small discount on their next order in exchange for rating their orders a certain number of times. This would encourage more customers to provide feedback, help gather information to enhance satisfaction, while also encouraging repeat purchases.

  • FoodHub should use demand forecasting to determine times where delivery will be most popular and provide more delivery personnel during that time and provide incentives for delivery personnel to work during those times.

  • FoodHub should use the popular cuisine (American food, Japanese Food, Italian Food), customer rating, and delivery performance to attract customers and feature these types of cuisines. Offer targeted promotions where discounts or deals are given from these restauarants. Along with the discounts from the restaurants, FoodHub should also provide discounts or deals by FoodHub on delivery of these types of cuisines.

  • FoodHub should try to reduce the delivery times on the weekdays. This will provide a more consistent and reliable experience and therefore bring more repeat customers. In general, improving the delivery time should be a point of emphasis.

  • FoodHub should monitor the restaurants with longer preparation times and help these restaurants identify ways to improve their preparation time.
